ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: <image>In the figure, $ m ∠1 = 3a + 40 $, $ m ∠2 = 2a + 25 $, and $ m ∠3 = 5b - 26 $. Find $a$.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two straight lines slanting upward to the right, and they have the same pink arrow markings, indicating that these two straight lines are parallel. An upper straight line slanting downward to the right intersects these two parallel lines at the same time, and angles 1 and 2 are marked near the two intersection points. Angles 1 and 2 are both located between the two parallel lines, and are on the same side of this transversal. Reasoning: Because angles 1 and 2 are same-side interior angles formed by parallel lines cut by the same transversal, they are supplementary, and their sum is 180 degrees. Given m∠1 = 3a + 40, m∠2 = 2a + 25, therefore (3a + 40) + (2a + 25) = 180. Combining gives 5a + 65 = 180, so 5a = 115, a = 23.
